knowledge-base.name: lang-typescript
knowledge-base.triggers: TypeScript, JavaScript, .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, tsconfig.json, package.json, Node.js, React, Vitest, Jest, ESLint, Prettier, Zod, Hono, Express, Koa, Vite, esbuild, tsx, ts-node
knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for TypeScript and JavaScript. Loaded automatically when agents work on .ts, .tsx, .js, or .jsx files. Applies to TypeScript 5+, Node.js 20+, ES2022+, React, and server-side JS.

core-principles.principle: Enable all strict flags; treat type errors as build failures. `strict: true` is non-negotiable.
Use `const`, `readonly`, `as const`, and spread operators. Mutate only when profiling demands it.
All function signatures, API responses, and public interfaces must have explicit type annotations. Infer internally.
Prefer pure functions, map/filter/reduce, and composition over classes and mutation.
Use `unknown` for truly unknown data, Zod/io-ts for runtime narrowing. Every `any` requires a code-review comment explaining why.

guardrail.rule: Never use `@ts-ignore`. Use `@ts-expect-error` with a justification comment instead.
guardrail.good: // @ts-expect-error: third-party lib missing types for overload (TODO: open PR upstream) someUntypedCall();

guardrail.rule: Every `catch` block must type-narrow the error before accessing properties. Never assume error shape.
Never create fire-and-forget promises without explicit `void` annotation. Always `await` or return promises.
Never use `var`. Never swallow errors with empty catch blocks. Never throw primitives.
Prefer `as const` objects over TypeScript `enum`. Enums produce runtime code and have surprising reverse-mapping behaviors.
Use `Promise.all` for independent concurrent operations. Never chain sequential `await` in a loop when order does not matter.
guardrail.good: // Concurrent const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([fetchUsers(), fetchPosts()]);

guardrail.rule: Set timeouts on all external calls (fetch, database, third-party APIs) using `AbortController`.
Use nullish coalescing (`??`) over logical OR (`||`) for defaults. `||` drops falsy values like `0`, `""`, and `false`.
guardrail.bad: const port = process.env.PORT || 3000; // breaks when PORT="0"

guardrail.rule: Never mix `.then()` chains with `await` in the same function. Pick one style per function.
Use ES module `import`/`export` exclusively. No `require()` in TypeScript files. Prefer named exports over default exports.
guardrail.bad: const express = require("express"); // CommonJS in TypeScript export default function myUtil() {} // default export hurts refactoring
guardrail.good: import express from "express"; export function myUtil() {}

guardrail.rule: Barrel exports (`index.ts`) only at package/feature boundaries. Not within internal modules — causes circular imports and tree-shaking failures.
Use `useError` chaining with `cause` option when re-throwing. Preserves the original stack trace.
guardrail.good: throw new AppError("Operation failed", "OP_FAILED", 500, { cause: originalError });

guardrail.rule: Side-effect imports must be documented with a comment explaining why they are needed.
guardrail.good: // Registers global error handlers and polyfills before app startup import "./setup";

tsconfig.description: Required tsconfig.json settings for strict TypeScript projects.
tsconfig.example: { "compilerOptions": { "strict": true, "target": "ES2022", "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "esModuleInterop": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true, "noImplicitReturns": true, "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true, "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true, "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true, "noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature": true, "isolatedModules": true, "verbatimModuleSyntax": true } }

flags.flag: Activates strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, and more
Arrays and records return T | undefined — forces null checks on array access
Distinguishes between missing property and property set to undefined
Ensures type-only imports are erased correctly — prevents runtime issues

directory.purpose: Validated environment variables using Zod schema
Business logic with zero I/O dependencies — pure functions, easy to test
Application services that orchestrate domain logic and I/O
Data access layer — database queries, external API calls
HTTP handlers and controllers — no business logic here

pattern.name: Custom Application Errors
pattern.context: All projects — define before writing service layer
pattern.description: Typed error hierarchy with machine-readable code and HTTP status code. Use `cause` for chaining.

pattern.name: Result Pattern
pattern.context: Expected failures — validation, parsing, domain rules — where throwing is too heavy
pattern.description: Discriminated union that forces callers to handle both success and failure paths at compile time. Avoids exception-for-control-flow anti-pattern.

pattern.name: Input Validation with Zod
pattern.context: All API boundaries and external data entry points
pattern.description: Runtime type narrowing at system boundaries. Derive TypeScript types from Zod schemas — single source of truth.

pattern.name: Validated Environment Variables
pattern.description: Parse and validate all env vars at startup using Zod. Fail fast with clear errors rather than undefined behavior at runtime.

pattern.name: Async Timeout with AbortController
pattern.context: Any external HTTP, database, or third-party API call
pattern.description: Every external call must have a timeout. Use AbortController to cancel in-flight requests.

rules.rule: Test files: co-located as `*.test.ts` or under `tests/` mirroring `src/`
Use `beforeEach` for setup; avoid `beforeAll` for mutable state
No `any` in test files; test helpers must be typed
Mock at boundaries (HTTP, database, file system) — not internal functions

eslint-config.description: Required ESLint rules for TypeScript projects (flat config format).

quick-reference.item: Forbidden — use `unknown` + Zod narrowing; every `any` needs a review comment
Use `as const` object + derived type instead of `enum`
Avoid — named exports improve refactoring and grep-ability
Always type `catch (e: unknown)` and narrow before accessing properties
Always `await` or `void`; never fire-and-forget without annotation
Use `Promise.all` for independent operations, not sequential awaits
Wrap all external calls with `AbortController` timeout
Use `??` not `||` to avoid false-negatives on `0`, `""`, `false`
Zod at all API and I/O boundaries; derive TS types from schemas
stdlib → external packages → internal modules → relative paths
index.ts only at package/feature boundaries, not internal modules
Vitest preferred over Jest for ESM-native projects
